aboutMore: ok serious random facts (the real ones): i work weekends at Captain Putt's Adventure Golf as the windmill guy on hole 7 (14 seconds per spin, i know it in my BONES). my grandma dot lives with us and is the only person who has ever given me a standing ovation (she was getting the gravy). my little brother jeremy is 9 and rates every bit i do on a scale of 1 to 10 in a notebook. highest score ever: a 6 (PIE, at assembly, into the principal's mic). i'm also in improv club on tuesdays, and my teacher told me i'm not random, i'm 'listening very fast.' i think about that every day. ninjas at school, pirates at work. dual citizen.

blog.title: HOLE SEVEN: a love story (the windmill post)
blog.body: i work saturdays and sundays at Captain Putt's Adventure Golf on the north end of town and my station is hole 7. the windmill. the blades go around every 14 SECONDS. i know it like u know ur own phone number. if u time the ball right it goes through the middle and rolls out the front. if u mistime it, it comes back and hits u in the shin and i say 'ARRR' out loud (that's in the contract) (so is the shirt). i keep a coat hanger in my back pocket because the windmill jams every 3rd sunday. a kid told me he got a hole in one on 7 and i said 'ONE?? on the WINDMILL??' and he said yes and i gave him a free token. there are no tokens. i invented one. it's a bottle cap. he has it now. i think it's the greatest thing i've ever created. better than the waffle thing. don't tell the waffle thing.

blog.title: my grandma dot is the only audience i need (also: jeremy's notebook)
blog.body: every night at dinner i do a show. 6 minutes. mostly bits. grandma dot (she's lived with us since spring) is the only person who's ever given me a standing ovation, and she was standing anyway, she was getting the gravy, BUT she looked right at me while she did it so it counts. my brother jeremy (9) rates every bit in a notebook. 412 bits so far. average score 3.2. highest ever: a 6, for saying PIE into the principal's mic. next to it he wrote 'good timing.' the lowest is a 1: 'ceiling fans are just helicopters that gave up.' next to it he wrote 'this one is actually kind of sad.' that's the best review i've ever gotten. i went to my room and thought about ceiling fans for an hour. i've read the notebook like 40 times. it's the only thing i own that's honest.

blog.title: yes, and (what i learned in improv club)
blog.body: i joined improv club (tuesdays, room 12, ms brandt) because i thought it was 'random with a permission slip.' first rule is YES AND. whatever your partner says, u say yes, and then u add something. so a girl said 'we're on a boat' and i said 'yes and the boat is full of pie.' ms brandt closed her eyes. fair. but in the next scene a girl named priya said 'i'm a lighthouse keeper and i'm lonely' and i didn't say anything random. i said 'yes. and i brought you a sandwich.' and the whole room went 'awww.' ms brandt stopped me after and said 'randy, you're not random. you listen very fast.' i have thought about it every day since. is that who i am. a listener. i'm not ready to say that out loud, so i'm typing it here. do NOT tell the cafeteria.

blog.title: THE INVISIBLE BAKE SALE: FINAL REPORT
blog.body: final numbers. attendance: 41 (nowhere). items sold: 0 (invisible). money raised: $0.00 (invisible) PLUS $38.50 (REAL) because people felt bad and handed me actual dollars for invisible pie. i didn't want to take it. a lady from my church put in a five. patrick mailed 2 dollars in an envelope that said 'for the pie. i could see it. it was apple.' walt sent a MONEY ORDER, for $5, with a letter that said 'a man should pay for what he was promised.' i couldn't tell him it was invisible. so i took it all to the animal shelter on Monroe St, where we got our cat Crumbs, and the lady asked what it was for. i said 'invisible apple pie.' she wrote it on the receipt. it says INVISIBLE APPLE PIE. the receipt is on my fridge. it's my greatest achievement. next sale: friday. location: nowhere. bring real money this time.
